sentences.text: Petitioner is the 3rd accused in Crime No.680 of 2024 of Anchal Police Station, Kollam.

He seeks to quash the FIR registered against him alleging offences under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 406 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

According to the defacto complainant, the accused had, with an intention to cheat, made him to believe that the vehicle bearing Registration No.KL-13-AE-7000 was available for sale for Rs.35,00,000/- and the amount was transferred to A1 and A2.

The 8 th accused complained that the vehicle was transferred without his knowledge and thereafter he transferred the vehicle back to the 8 th accused and sustained a loss of Rs.50,00,000/- and the accused conspired to cheat the defacto complainant by the above acts, thereby committing the offences alleged.

3. Adv.S.Krishna, appearing for the petitioner contended that petitioner is only a broker in the transaction and that he has no involvement other than acting as an agent to connect the willing purchaser to a willing seller and that he is unaware of the commission of any forgery or cheating as alleged.
It was also contended that the uncontroverted allegations in the FIR would not make out any of the CRL.MC NO. 8370 OF 2024 2024:KER:75285 offences alleged.

4. Smt.Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor on the other hand submitted that the petition to quash the proceedings filed by the 8 th accused has already been dismissed by this Court after observing that the matter requires investigation.

It was further submitted that the involvement of the petitioner is a matter which can be identified only after investigation and hence scuttling such probe at the initial stage itself would cause serious prejudice.
5.
The FIR was registered only on 08.06.2024.
The 8 th accused had already approached this Court contending that he is innocent.
However, this Court declined to interfere with the FIR, having regard to the nature of offences and the allegations contained therein.
The same FIR is now under challenge by the 3 rd accused.

The exact role of the 3 rd accused can be revealed only during Subair Muhammad vs The State Of Kerala on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197870503/
2 investigation.

sentences.text: The uncontroverted allegations do initiate the offences alleged.
Therefore, it is too premature a stage for this Court to interfere under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

Accordingly, I dismiss this Crl.M.C. Sd/-
